caption:
Lulu went from short commutes to a big weekend group ride, and her back felt cranky afterwards.

Cycling keeps your back bent forward for a long time. Most backs handle it well, but a big jump in ride time can outpace your capacity.

Build ride time and hills gradually. Change hand positions and stand on climbs now and then. If you tweak your saddle height or reach, make one change at a time. Off the bike, hip and trunk strength work like bridges and side planks twice a week can help your back tolerate longer rides.

Changes to bladder or bowel control, or numbness around the groin, need urgent medical care. Our Chatswood and Sydney CBD physios can help. Book online via the link in bio 🚴
